The Asterline ferry sails between the mainland port of Kessow and the island town of Brava.
The crossing covers 58 kilometres and takes three and a half hours.
The service started in 1926 with a single steamship that carried mail and cattle.
The current ship, launched in 2012, has room for 900 passengers and 160 cars.
There are two sailings a day in summer and one in winter.
Storms cancel about one sailing in fifteen between December and February.
Islanders pay half the normal fare, a discount that dates from 1950.
A plan to replace the ferry with a tunnel was rejected by voters in 2008.

source_text: Fourteen months is the shortest permitted ageing time for a wheel, which comes to around six kilograms. People often compare the crumbly texture to fudge, and the taste is both sharp and faintly sweet. Since 1996 the right to call a cheese Saltmere has been limited by law to nine farms. Roughly 70 tonnes are made each year in total, mostly for sale on the mainland. Islanders usually pair it with dark rye bread and sliced pear. A five-year-old wheel took first place at the 2019 Northern Dairy Awards.

On the island of Tamor, the active volcano Mount Seregal rises to 3,470 metres.
Nineteen eruptions have been recorded since 1640, when records started.
In 1883 the biggest eruption covered the town of Old Leru with four metres of ash.
Coffee and vanilla are grown on the lower slopes, where the soil is rich.
When gas activity rises, the crater lake at the top turns from green to grey.
The volcano is watched by scientists using 26 sensors which detect slight ground movements.
Its latest eruption in 2014 made 12,000 residents abandon their homes for two months.
A permit and a local guide are required for the climb, which lasts two days.

Four lanes wide, the Ravensholm Bridge has spanned the Tarn estuary ever since its 1987 opening.
No cable-stayed structure in the area could match the 1,240 metres of its principal span on completion.
Marta Elvanne, the lead engineer, modelled both towers on masts from the vanished herring fleet.
After six years of work, the final bill reached some 310 million crowns, close to double the initial estimate.
In the days before the bridge, a forty-minute ferry ride in calm conditions was the sole option.
Lorries and buses are turned away around twelve days annually because of dangerous winds.
The charge is three crowns, and it applies solely to vehicles travelling north.
Once a year in May, a morning race gives thousands of runners the chance to cross without traffic.
candidate_text:
• The Ravensholm Bridge opened in 1987 and carries four lanes of traffic across the Tarn estuary.
  • Its main span measures 1,240 metres, which made it the longest cable-stayed crossing in the region at the time.
  • Engineer Marta Elvanne designed the two towers to resemble the masts of the old herring fleet.
  • Construction took six years and cost roughly 310 million crowns, almost double the original budget.
  • Before the bridge existed, the only way across was a ferry that took forty minutes in good weather.
  • High winds close the bridge to tall vehicles about twelve days each year.
  • A toll of three crowns is collected only from traffic heading north.
  • Every May, the road is closed for a morning so that thousands of runners can cross it on foot.

Mature trees grow to 45 metres tall and may live for over 600 years.
The wood is nearly black and dense enough to sink in water.
Because it resists sea worms and rot, shipbuilders used it for keels over many centuries.
Growth is slow, with the trunk gaining only around two millimetres per year.
Around 90 percent of the old trees were cut down by intensive logging during the nineteenth century.
Since 1978 felling has been against the law, though fallen trees may still be gathered.
